parallel-distributed processing is the most plausible mechanism for associative learning in PC, and that the architecture of PC and other cortical areas can be understood in terms of principles that govern associative processes in the mammalian brain.
the olfactory system provides an unparalleled opportunity for the experimental study and theoretical analysis of parallel-distributed processing.

parallel-distributed processing in PC, like that in other cortical areas, is based on a combination of feedforward and feedback connectivity, and is mediated by a combination of synaptic and intrinsic membrane mechanisms.

PC is a model of associative processes in the brain that is accessible to a variety of experimental, theoretical and modeling approaches.
the olfactory system, and particularly PC and related cortical structures, is an excellent system for studying parallel-distributed processes and their neural implementation in the mammalian brain.
